messages:
infra-bot: Alert: sudden conntrack table spike in az-us-east-1b on GPU pool nodes. nf_conntrack_count ~1.6M, nf_conntrack_max=1.8M. Observed pod -> external failures and retries. PagerDuty: oncall.
maya: seeing training jobs in gpu-trainers namespace fail to pull checkpoints and to push metrics. errors: "connection reset", "i/o timeout". Affected jobs restart loop.
chris: grabbed node metrics, example from gpu-node-17:
```bash
# conntrack -S | egrep 'entries' -A2
# nf_conntrack_count: 1623400
# nf_conntrack_max: 1800000
```
lots of short-lived TCP connections to our artifact service + S3. High SYN/FIN churn.
maya: also seeing a ton of ephemeral port reuse on nodes, netstat shows many TIME_WAIT sockets.
toni: quick triage — is this SNAT churn from centralized NAT gateway or per-node SNAT? If pods are being SNATed through a small pool that's a bad combo with many short TCP flows.
chris: cluster uses kube-proxy (iptables) + CNI overlay. Egress goes via per-AZ NAT instances for tenant VPC egress. Looks like clients on pods open many parallel short connections -> conntrack entries pile up.
liam: tried bumping nf_conntrack_max to 2.5M on one AZ's gpu nodes as a canary (sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=2500000). After ~5m the error rate dropped and checkpoint fetches resumed.
samir: can we also reduce conntrack timeouts to free entries faster? current tcp_established timeout is 432000 (5 days) which is way too long for short flows.
toni: suggested quick changes:
 - sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=2500000
 - sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=300
 - increase ephemeral port range: sysctl net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range="10240 65535"
Applied to canary nodes and rolling out now.
devops-oncall: applied timeout/port-range changes to 6 nodes in az-us-east-1b. Observed nf_conntrack_count drop to ~180k within 10m and job failures stopped.
maya: nice. Short-term mitigation worked. But this is a band-aid — we should fix root cause.
chris: root cause hypothesis: GPU training jobs open lots of short-lived connections to S3/artifact service for many small files. SNAT per-AZ NAT instance has less connection capacity than aggregate pod churn.
liam: long-term options:
 - move artifact pulls to keepalive/connection pooling (patch training launcher)
 - shift artifact traffic through an internal egress gateway that preserves source IPs (avoid centralized NAT bottleneck)
 - enable node-local SNAT (ensure per-node SNAT via ipvs or CNI settings) or use IP-per-pod so no SNAT
 - add conntrack autoscaling & alerting (ct_count/ct_utilization)
samir: also add a pre-deploy load test for gpu pool that simulates short-lived many-connections workload.
toni: I'll open infra PR with sysctl daemonset + cluster-operator change to make ephemeral range & reduced timeouts default for gpu nodes, and add alert rule: conntrack_utilization > 0.6 for 5m -> page.
devops-oncall: ticket INFRA-2147 created, assigning to @toni. Also scheduled emergency capacity increase for NAT instances for the next 2 hours until we roll configs globally.
maya: will follow up with a small change in trainer to reuse HTTP keepalive for artifact downloads.
chris: logging note: capture conntrack rates (new entries/sec) in node exporter to detect spikes rather than absolute only.
liam: postmortem action items:
 - PR for sysctl daemonset and k8s node config
 - egress design doc for preserving source IPs or adding per-AZ autoscaling NAT
 - code change in trainer to pool connections
 - load test + runbook
closing: page resolved, monitoring OK in az-us-east-1b. We'll roll to other AZs tomorrow.
